reference: No matching GNU pcap-info/capture CLI is available in the pinned inventory (tcpdump is marked missing). Runnable contracts use manually byte-encoded classic pcap fixtures based on the independent version-2.4 file-format layout and the documented pcap info output; metadata cases use Bash's documented type/help builtins. Packet-capture behavior is deferred pending an isolated privileged VM or AF_PACKET mock.
coverage: Bash builtin availability and documented help metadata
pcap info on empty and multi-record little-endian classic pcap files
swapped-endian microsecond and little-endian nanosecond pcap headers
recognized linktype names and accumulated captured-payload byte count
rejection of invalid magic and incomplete global/record framing
rejection of record payloads shorter than incl_len
exclusions: No GNU parity cases: the pinned loadables inventory names tcpdump as the counterpart but marks it missing, and Bash does not provide the pcap loadable in reference mode.

Live capture, interface binding, packet-count/snaplen behavior, timeout behavior, output record timestamps, and CAP_NET_RAW capability handling require controlled packet injection and an isolated privileged VM or AF_PACKET mock.

cases.purpose: Check Bash type metadata identifies pcap as a loadable builtin; this is availability metadata, not operation coverage.
Check Bash help metadata contains the documented capture synopsis, info verb, and short description; this is metadata, not operation coverage.
cases.script:
doc=$(help pcap)
[[ $doc == *'pcap [-i IFACE] -w FILE'* ]]
[[ $doc == *'Packet capture writer (libpcap classic file format).'* ]]
[[ $doc == *'pcap info FILE'* ]]
printf 'documented pcap help entries present\n'

cases.purpose: Check the documented info summary for a zero-record little-endian microsecond classic pcap with Ethernet linktype and snaplen 64.
cases.stdout:
file:     empty.pcap
magic:    0xa1b2c3d4
version:  2.4
snaplen:  64
linktype: 1 (EN10MB)
records:  0
payload:  0 bytes

cases.purpose: Check record walking and payload accounting on two valid records, including an incl_len smaller than orig_len and a NUL payload byte.
cases.stdout:
file:     records.pcap
magic:    0xa1b2c3d4
version:  2.4
snaplen:  64
linktype: 1 (EN10MB)
records:  2
payload:  5 bytes

cases.purpose: Check decoding of a standard swapped-endian microsecond header and record length, including the RAW linktype label.
cases.stdout:
file:     swapped.pcap
magic:    0xd4c3b2a1 (swapped endian)
version:  2.4
snaplen:  64
linktype: 101 (RAW)
records:  1
payload:  1 bytes

cases.purpose: Check acceptance of the classic pcap nanosecond-resolution magic and a recognized Linux cooked linktype.
cases.stdout:
file:     nano.pcap
magic:    0xa1b23c4d
version:  2.4
snaplen:  128
linktype: 113 (LINUX_SLL)
records:  0
payload:  0 bytes

cases.purpose: Check rejection of a full-sized global header whose magic field is not any recognized classic pcap byte order or timestamp resolution.
Check that a file shorter than the required 24-byte global pcap header is reported as malformed.
Check that an incomplete 16-byte per-record header fails after the valid global metadata is read.
cases.stdout:
file:     short-record.pcap
magic:    0xa1b2c3d4
version:  2.4
snaplen:  64
linktype: 1 (EN10MB)

cases.purpose: Require info to reject a record that declares three captured bytes but contains only one, as classic pcap framing requires incl_len payload bytes. This catches a real parser compatibility gap if the record walk skips beyond EOF.
cases.script:
printf '\324\303\262\241\002\000\004\000\000\000\000\000\000\000\000\000\100\000\000\000\001\000\000\000' > short-payload.pcap
printf '\001\000\000\000\002\000\000\000\003\000\000\000\003\000\000\000a' >> short-payload.pcap
status=0
pcap_output=$(pcap info short-payload.pcap 2>short-payload.err) || status=$?
diagnostic=$(<short-payload.err)
if [[ $status -ne 1 || -z $diagnostic ]]; then printf 'truncated payload check mismatch: status=%d stderr-length=%d' "$status" "${#diagnostic}" >&2; exit 1; fi
printf '%s' 'truncated payload rejected'

cases.purpose: Capture a known frame count into a classic pcap file and verify global and per-record fields, snaplen truncation, and output permissions.
cases.reason: Requires CAP_NET_RAW plus deterministic Ethernet frame injection on a private isolated link, or a reviewed AF_PACKET mock. A future disposable VM must inject fixed frame bytes, run capture with bounded -c/-s/-W settings, and independently decode the resulting pcap; no host interface or real network target is in scope.

cases.purpose: Check interface selection and bounded timeout behavior with and without injected packets.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable VM with a private test interface that can be selected by name and driven by a controlled packet source while holding CAP_NET_RAW. A future fixture should verify only frames from that interface are written and that -W terminates the no-traffic case within a bounded interval.
